description: Split it. Ship it. Track it - Because every big job deserves a little scherry on top :cherries:

summary.one_liner: scherry is a Go library for distributed job orchestration that splits a large job into parallel tasks, fans them out over Kafka, and persists job and task state in PostgreSQL with a built-in history web console.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a two-level job-to-task model: a JobExecutor splits work into a list of TaskData items, each persisted as a task and published as a Kafka message, and a TaskExecutor processes each one. Cron-based job triggering uses Asynq with Redis, while Kafka topics handle task fan-out, a retry topic with configurable delay, and a dead-letter topic for exhausted tasks. Jobs and tasks move through an explicit state machine, and a job is finalized automatically once all its tasks reach a terminal state, checked on a configurable cron. Jobs can be scheduled or fired manually via Trigger, and RetryJob re-queues failed tasks. An embedded web console on its own port shows progress, timings, retry lineage, and upcoming scheduled runs, backed by Postgres. Execution hooks (OnTasksPublished, OnTaskStarted, OnTaskFinished, OnJobFinished) allow custom instrumentation such as Prometheus metrics.
use_cases: split a large batch job into parallel tasks
scheduled payroll or bulk payout runs
track progress and failures of batch jobs
retry failed batch tasks via Kafka
on-demand job triggered from an HTTP handler
monitor job history in a web console
how_to_run: Apply migrations from migrations/ to PostgreSQL (partitioned scherry_jobs and scherry_tasks tables)
Run Redis for Asynq scheduler/worker and Kafka for task fan-out
Create a service with scherry.New(scherry.Config{...}) and call Register or RegisterManual with JobConfig
Call svc.Start(ctx, mux) and run an asynq.NewServer(...).Run(mux) worker
Optionally start the history console with svc.StartConsole(":3002")
notable: Two-level job-to-task model with automatic job finalization once all tasks settle
Kafka fan-out for tasks with retry topic and dead-letter topic
Durable PostgreSQL history with execution timing and retry lineage
RegisterShared lets multiple jobs share one Kafka consumer and TaskExecutor to bound downstream load
Embedded history console with overview, history, jobs, and upcoming tabs
caveats: The history console has no built-in authentication and must be protected in production
Duplicate-run suppression via refID is best-effort; concurrent triggers can still create multiple runs
Requires three external services to run: PostgreSQL, Redis, and Kafka
Shared consumers share failure domain and throughput; a long retry delay on one job can hold up others
